title: Real Madrid Player Ratings vs. Villarreal: Vinicius Junior Red Card Overshadows Crucial Win
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell5:23 PM EDTVinícius Júnior (center) was handed his marching orders in the second half. / Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesReal Madrid squeaked out a 1–0 victory over Villarreal on Saturday, persevering with 10 men after Vinícius Júnior was sent off in the 74th minute.

When Los Blancos kicked off under the lights at the Bernabéu, the team was nine points behind La Liga leaders Barcelona. Collecting three points was absolutely imperative for José Mourinho’s men in their return to domestic action, but the only thing they produced in the first half were thousands of whistles from the home crowd.

Yan Diomande finally gave the fans something to cheer when he bagged his first goal to put the hosts up 1–0 in the 62nd minute. The teenager collected a clever ball from Federico Valverde on the turn and then fired a right-footed strike into the back of the net.

Vinícius Jr was the next man on the scoresheet nine minutes later, but a VAR review chopped off the goal for a foul in the build-up. The replay showed the Brazil international pull the hair of Nathan Saliba before he was off to the races and was promptly shown a red card, leaving Real Madrid down to 10 men.

The 15-time European champions dug deep and saw out the win, withstanding a flurry of chances from Villarreal to bring the gap to Barcelona back to six points. The win hardly felt like a triumph, though, given how the game turned in the final stages.

Yan Diomande delivered when Real Madrid needed it most. / Alvaro Medranda/Quality Sport Images/Getty ImagesMourinho turned heads when he benched Vinícius Jr for Saturday’s clash. The decision could have simply been because the winger logged heavy minutes during the international break for Brazil and also had to travel back to Spain from India. But there was no ignoring just how poorly the No. 7 has played for club and country in 2026–27.

Yan Diomande instead got the nod on the left wing. The stage was set for the blockbuster summer signing to make a statement in the rare opportunity, but apart from a few blistering runs forward, there wasn’t much to celebrate about his opening 45 minutes.

Mourinho could sense the team was in desperate need of a boost as the game unfolded scoreless, so he introduced Vinícius Jr in the 52nd minute. But instead of replacing Diomande, the Portuguese boss moved the teenager to the right wing—and it paid off 10 minutes later.

Diomande buried a clinical finish and then Vinícius Jr soon doubled Real Madrid’s lead. It looked like the attack was finally finding its footing after a lackluster start to the season ... but Vinícius Jr’s goal was wiped away and he was sent off.

The team went from a group hug around Vinícius Jr to a group attack on the referee. What could have been a turning point for the winger—and the frontline—this season is now just another moment shrouded in controversy.

GK: Thibaut Courtois—8.2: Could have gone for a stroll around Spain in the first half and no one would have noticed. Called into action more after the restart and had to stand on his head to keep a clean sheet.

RB: Trent Alexander-Arnold—7.0: Delivered sensational service to Mbappé. A bright spot pushing forward on a team that looked all out of ideas for long stretches. Harshly taken out of the game early in the second half.
CB: Ibrahima Konaté—7.3: Played without any signs of a lingering injury. Continues to deliver a solid debut campaign. Read danger well, especially when the team went down to 10 men.

CB: Antonio Rüdiger—7.9: Turned back the clock to step up in Huijsen’s absence. Always the one making a timely clearance or shutting down a promising sequence from the visitors. Won all but one of his duels.
LB: Álvaro Carreras—7.1: Time on the bench has done him well. Looked sharp from the opening whistle and linked up well with Diomande down the left. Didn’t deserve to come off at halftime.

DM: Federico Valverde—8.2: Started the game in midfield, then went out to the right wing and  ended up at right back all before the game reached the hour-mark. Guess where he was at his best?The position he hates playing.
DM: Aurélien Tchouaméni—7.2: Tidy in possession and crucial in defense. Enjoyed more progressive passing, continuously looking to get the ball into the final third.
RW: Arda Güler—6.9: Not one of his better outings on the wing. Eventually dropped into midfield to try and dictate the flow of play for his side with mixed results.
